_howToUpdate: Edit this file only — never index.html. Each entry carries its own 'checked' date (YYYY-MM-DD): the day YOU last opened the organizer's own page and confirmed it. Re-check an entry, update its 'checked'. The page prints the OLDEST check across all entries, so it can only overstate staleness, never understate it. An entry past 30 days shows its age in red — that is the nudge to re-check or remove it. 'deadline' is the last day it is useful; null for programs with no closing date. 'opens' is for programs whose window has not started yet — they sit in 'Opens later' and move themselves into 'Open now' on that date. Anything past its deadline moves itself to 'Recently closed' automatically.

entries.what: The 40-hour Army Corps of Engineers Safety and Health Requirements course, live on Zoom. Stricter than OSHA in places that matter: lower fall-protection triggers, formal Activity Hazard Analyses, submittal steps OSHA never asks for.
facts: Monday 19 – Friday 23 October 2026 · 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM Pacific daily
Open to everyone — veterans, active duty, contractors, civilians

This course does not by itself make you a Site Safety and Health Officer. EM 385-1-1 requires an SSHO to have five years of consecutive construction safety supervision (four with CHST, CSP, ASP or OHST), an OSHA 30 card, and eight hours of documented CE a year. The 40-hour course is not named in the manual as an SSHO qualification — it became a de facto standard because contracts started requiring it.
If you have VR&E, WIOA or state workforce funding, ask whether this course qualifies before you put $350 on a card.

entries.what: Explore Pathways to Cyber Careers — a live session on how certifications map to actual cyber roles, and what to build alongside them.
facts: Friday, 23 October 2026 · 12:00–1:30 PM Pacific / 3:00–4:30 PM Eastern
Dr. James Stanger, Chief Technology Evangelist, CompTIA
Veterans, active duty, Guard and Reserve, military spouses and military families
Free. Five attendees receive a CompTIA certification voucher.

entries.what: The 30-hour OSHA Construction card, live on Zoom across two weekends. If you are building toward an SSHO role, this is the one actually named in the EM 385-1-1 requirement — take it before the 40-hour course, not after.
facts: Saturday 24 – Sunday 25 October, then Saturday 31 October – Sunday 1 November 2026 · from 8:00 AM
A second Construction run goes 16–19 November 2026, and an OSHA 30 General Industry run goes 14–15 and 21–22 November — both $250, same organizer.

entries.what: An in-person hiring event for cleared professionals, run by ClearedJobs.Net.
facts: Hyatt Regency, 2300 Dulles Corner Boulevard, Herndon, VA
This is a CI or FS polygraph event. Without one of those you will not get in the door — check the event page before you drive.
Printed résumés and your clearance details. Dress as you would for an interview; these are real interviews, not a meet-and-greet.

entries.what: The next ClearedJobs.Net cleared hiring event after Herndon, same format.
facts: The Hotel, 7795 Arundel Mills Blvd, Hanover, MD
CI or FS polygraph event, same as Herndon.

entries.what: No-cost, live, one-to-one online tutoring and homework help, funded by the Department of Defense. 24/7, more than 150 subjects, kindergarten through college.
facts: Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, Coast Guard and DoD civilians — active duty, Reserve and National Guard including part-time drilling status, plus Survivor and Wounded Warrior. Dependants qualify when the service member is in a qualifying status.
Homework help in math, science, reading and writing; live essay review; SAT and ACT prep; study skills; parent coaching
Spanish-language help in math, science, social studies, writing and study skills — and Spanish parent coaching, for the adult sitting next to the kid doing the homework
Free to eligible users. No appointment, no waiting list, any internet-connected device.

Veterans are not named as an eligible status on their own, and former DoD civilians who no longer work for DoD are specifically not eligible. If you have separated, read the eligibility table before you plan around this.
Tutor.com states the program depends on available budget and is not guaranteed — funders set eligibility and it can change.

Tutor.com also appears inside the DoD MWR digital library collection, where it carries its own eligibility rules on top of the library's. Two different doors with two different rule sets — if one turns you away, the other may not. See the DoD MWR Digital Library entry on this list.

entries.what: Free self-paced Salesforce and AI training on Trailhead, plus certification exam vouchers that cover the roughly $200 exam fee.
facts: Current and transitioning service members, their spouses, and veterans of all eras who served in the US, Canada, UK, Australia or New Zealand. Gold Star Children in the US were added recently. Guard and Reserve are not named in the eligibility wording — ask the program before you plan around it.
Self-paced Trailhead training, optional virtual Trailhead Academy classes with fees waived, and 1:1 career coaching through non-profit partners
A certification exam voucher, plus one retake voucher per certification on request
You can apply for the Hiring Our Heroes 12-week fellowship and get guaranteed interviews through the Salesforce Talent Alliance
Class registration must be completed within 7 days of approval, exam vouchers expire, and exam accommodation requests need 30 days' notice.

entries.what: A free lifetime America the Beautiful pass covering entrance and standard day-use fees at federal recreation sites. No VA disability rating required, and no closing date.
facts: Veterans of any branch, including National Guard and Reserve, plus Gold Star Family members
National Park Service, Forest Service, Fish & Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation and Army Corps of Engineers sites
The holder plus occupants of one private non-commercial vehicle, or two motorcycles. Where fees are per person, the holder plus three others aged 16 and over.
Veteran Health Identification Card, the VA's digital Veteran ID Card, DD Form 2, DD Form 2765, Next Generation USID, or a veteran designation on a state driver's licence or ID card
Free in person at many federal recreation sites. Free as a digital pass on Recreation.gov; $7.50 for a physical card posted to you, or $10 by mail from the USGS Store.
A separate free Access Pass exists for any US citizen or resident with a permanent disability, and can discount expanded amenities such as camping and guided tours.
entries.linkLabel: nps.gov — veterans and Gold Star families free access

entries.what: A one-time free year of LinkedIn Premium for the military community. Worth knowing before you chase it: as of this check the programme is being restructured, and LinkedIn's own page no longer describes a direct way to claim it.
facts: LinkedIn's page says the programme is being updated to distribute subscriptions through selected non-profit partners, and tells people to check back. There is no self-serve claim path described on it right now.

Eligible US service members and veterans, and their spouses, as LinkedIn determines. You must also be enrolled in an approved career training programme and hold no Premium subscription when you redeem.
Twelve months of Job Seeker Career Premium, one time, running from the day you redeem it

No. LinkedIn states that after the one-year promotional period the subscription terminates — you will not be billed at full rate when it ends. Several third-party write-ups claim otherwise; LinkedIn's own page is the one to trust.

entries.org: Think GREAT Foundation — Military Spouse Scholarship
entries.what: An academic scholarship for military and veteran spouses. The window has not opened yet — this is here so you can get documents together before January, not so you can apply today.
facts: Spouses of US service members and veterans, married to them during the service member's service
Enrolled or planning to enrol at a community college, college or university accredited by the US Department of Education, or in a certificate, licensure or technical programme
$2,500 per academic year, with a $10,000 lifetime maximum per applicant

Funds go directly to the financial institution and cannot exceed the actual unmet need on your student account. Anything left over is retained by the foundation and may be applied to another semester in the same academic year.
Maintain a 3.0 GPA and satisfactory progress toward the degree

entries.org: Coalition to Salute America's Heroes — Emergency Financial Aid
entries.what: Help with urgent bills for a narrow slice of post-9/11 veterans. The eligibility is far tighter than the name suggests, and it is worth reading before you start.
facts: OEF or OIF veterans who served boots-on-the-ground in Iraq or Afghanistan, were injured there, and are rated 30% or more for a single injury — not a combined rating. Honorable discharge required.
First-time applicants only. If you have received aid from them before, you are not eligible again.
Utilities, rent or mortgage, auto loan, groceries, baby formula, household and school supplies. Not auto repairs or home repairs — those get advocacy only.
csah.webauthor.com/go/apply.cfm — the application link on their own Get Help page does not resolve, so use this one.
They publish no dollar amount and no processing time. Funds are limited and aid is not guaranteed.

entries.what: Short-term help with housing, utilities, food and transport for military families. The application only accepts submissions during a ten-day window each month.
facts: Applications open on the 1st and close at 11:59 PM Central on the 10th, every month. Nothing submitted outside it is reviewed.
Post-9/11 wounded, ill or injured in the line of duty, within 10 years of separation, honorable or general discharge.
E-1 to E-6 with DEERS-eligible dependents: currently deployed with Hostile Fire Pay, at sea 30+ days, unaccompanied overseas PCS, or Guard/Reserve on Title 10 orders.
E-1 to E-6 active duty with DEERS dependents — this track covers food assistance and dependents' vision care only.
Rent and mortgage, utilities, auto payments and insurance, food, essential home items, medical, travel, critical baby items.
A caseworker calls to verify. Reviews happen after the window closes; no processing time is published.

entries.what: Financial assistance and supply kits for veterans hit by a disaster. The most open door of the financial-help programs — no membership and no disability rating required.
facts: Ill, injured or wounded veterans and their spouses in the same household, plus qualifying surviving spouses including those of former Prisoners of War.
No DAV membership required and no service-connected compensation required.
Either an isolated or a large-scale disaster — an individual house fire counts, not only federally declared events.
Financial assistance plus supply kits: backpacks, blankets and hygiene kits.
Through a local DAV office or benefits advocate — there is no online application form.
One per family, per disaster. No dollar amount is published.

entries.what: A one-time grant for a recent crisis. The name reads as officers-only and it is not — their own page says all ranks and branches, which is why most people skip it.
facts: All ranks and branches. Active duty including Guard and Reserve, veterans with honorable or general discharge, spouses, surviving spouses, and caregivers of eligible service members or veterans.
The crisis must have happened within the past 12 months, you must show financial need, and you must not have a prior felony conviction.
A one-time grant up to $1,000. One grant per person, per household. Receipts due within 30 days.
Housing, utilities, auto, medical and insurance, and other critical needs. Not legal fees or child support.
Decision generally in 7–14 business days, then 5–7 days to disburse.

A second MOAA page describes this as relief for a natural disaster or national emergency, while the program page sets no such limit. Call 800-234-6622 or email relief@moaa.org to confirm your situation qualifies before applying.

entries.org: HOPE For The Warriors — Critical Needs Assistance
entries.what: Rent, mortgage or utility payments plus case management. Post-9/11 only, and explicitly not emergency aid — their own page says to allow three to four weeks.
facts: Post-9/11 only — service members, veterans, military spouses, caregivers and family members. Also veterans experiencing homelessness and survivors of military sexual trauma.
Their own wording: support may take 3–4 weeks to process. If you need money this week, start elsewhere and let this run in parallel.
Rent, mortgage or utilities, paid direct, plus case management, financial education and referrals.
Home or vehicle purchases, down payments, child support, credit card debt, legal fees, service animals, auto repairs, or medical and mental-health treatment.
Short form through Connect to Services, then an intake call where eligibility is confirmed.
No dollar limit, lifetime limit or waiting period is published.

entries.what: Adapted homes, home modifications, adapted vehicles and mobility devices. The gate here is injury severity, not a disability rating — most veterans with a rating will not qualify.
facts: Severely wounded or catastrophically injured veterans and first responders. A service-connected rating on its own does not qualify you, and the foundation publishes no numeric threshold to self-screen against.
Smart homes predominantly support post-9/11 defenders. Home modifications and mobility devices are open to veterans of every conflict.
Mortgage-free custom adapted smart homes, modifications to an existing home such as accessible bathrooms, kitchens and ramps, plus adapted vehicles and mobility devices.
One application form reached through their contact page, which routes by whether you are a veteran, first responder or family member. Phone (615) 575-3500.
106 homes completed since 2011, 12 under construction. No waiting-list policy or processing time is published.

entries.org: Bob Hope Critical Financial Assistance Program
entries.what: Run by the Elizabeth Dole Foundation. The caregiver applies, not the veteran — and unlike most programs on this list, it has no service-era restriction.
facts: The caregiver applies, not the veteran. Adults 18 and over providing care to a wounded, ill or injured veteran or service member — any era. Survivors who provided care within the last 12 months are included.
Household income must generally be $150,000 or below, with consideration for extraordinary or life-altering circumstances.
Housing, utilities, transportation and household stability. Paid straight to the vendor, so you will need a W-9 from them — getting it early prevents delays.
4–6 weeks before the team contacts you to schedule an intake call, and 6–8 weeks from application to payment. Open continuously, no deadline.
Email resourcenavigation@elizabethdolefoundation.org with Urgent Support in the subject line rather than waiting on the form.
Previous applicants may apply again if new or extraordinary circumstances arise. Everyone eligible gets resource navigation whether or not they are funded.

entries.org: ACT Now Education — Weekly Rundown: Nondestructive Testing
entries.what: A free virtual session on Nondestructive Testing — finding cracks and flaws inside aircraft, bridges, pipelines and reactors without cutting anything open. Covers what the field is, who is hiring, the training ladder, and how military inspection experience transfers.
facts: Saturday, 24 October 2026 · 1:00 PM Eastern · 12:00 Central · 11:00 Mountain · 10:00 Pacific
Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses

If you held an NDI billet, worked QA, or signed off inspections in any service, you have already done a version of this work — industry runs on the same standards. If you did not, NDT is one of the few fields where a certification ladder rather than a degree decides what you earn.

David Sanders, ASNT Level III and NAS 410 Level III, NDT instructor and consultant · Dr. Ronnie D. Ingram, DM, MBA, MBE, retired USMC Master Sergeant, QA professional and university adjunct · Muriel D. Magloire, Senior Quality Manager, QC Engineering, GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy
What NDT is · career opportunities across industries · training and advancement pathways · how military skills map across · mentorship and how to get connected
The Weekly Rundown runs weekly. If you cannot make this one, registering is how you hear about the next.

entries.org: Service to Success — Career Transition Cohort
entries.what: A free four-session career transition programme run across two weeks, ending the day before their virtual hiring fair. Résumé help, interview coaching, mentorship, networking, a hiring fair, a mastermind group and an exam voucher raffle. You apply to it rather than sign up for it.
facts: Tuesday 3, Thursday 5, Tuesday 10 and Thursday 12 November 2026 · 7:00–8:30 PM Eastern
The published times do not name a zone. Both organisations publish in Eastern, so Eastern is the working assumption — confirm it on your confirmation email before blocking the evenings.
Active duty, transitioning service members, veterans, National Guard and Reserve, and military spouses
Résumé help · interview coaching · mentorship · networking · a hiring fair · a mastermind group · an exam voucher raffle

Twelve required questions, not a sign-up form. Have ready: the job title you are targeting, your target salary range, where you want to work and whether you will relocate, when you can start, and a written answer on why you want a place. Give it fifteen minutes.

The final question asks whether you are prepared to complete assignments, attend sessions, respond to opportunities and take action throughout the programme. One answer option is that you have scheduling limitations. Four evenings with work in between — answer it honestly.
The cohort ends Thursday 12 November. Service to Success runs a virtual military hiring fair on Friday 13 November — four nights of résumé and interview work, then recruiters the next day.
ACT Now Education, not the Service to Success site.

entries.org: USO × U.S. Secret Service — Career Opportunities
entries.what: A free one-hour virtual session with a U.S. Secret Service recruiter on careers across the agency and how military experience maps to them.
facts: Tuesday 3 November 2026 · 11:00 AM Eastern · 10:00 Central · 9:00 Mountain · 8:00 Pacific
Daylight saving ends Sunday 1 November, two days before. Anything worked out from a daylight-time figure lands an hour off. Your Zoom confirmation shows the start in your own zone — trust that.

Active duty, veterans, retirees, military spouses, National Guard and Reservists. The short audience line on USO material usually reads as currently-serving only, but the registration form takes all of these — pick your affiliation and register.
The Secret Service is not only special agents — Uniformed Division, technical and engineering roles, intelligence analysis, finance and administration all sit inside the agency.

Bring two or three specific questions written down. Federal hiring has its own language — series and grade, specialised experience, referral lists — and a recruiter will answer those in plain English.

entries.what: A free two-hour virtual workshop on federal résumés and how federal hiring actually works, led by Keith Cassant, Veterans Federal Program Manager. Offered through the USO Financial Wellness program.
facts: Tuesday 17 November 2026 · 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM Eastern · 10:00 Central · 9:00 Mountain · 8:00 Pacific

Active duty, veterans, retirees, military spouses, National Guard and Reservists. The short audience line on USO material usually reads as currently-serving only, but the registration form takes all of these — pick your affiliation and register.
How to strengthen your federal résumé · what hiring managers are really looking for · how the federal hiring process works · why networking matters and how to use it

It wants hours per week, supervisor names and contact details, salary, and month-and-year dates — detail a civilian résumé strips out. A human rater scores you against the specialised experience in the announcement, so leaving it out gets a qualified application screened out on a technicality.
Bring an actual résumé you have already sent somewhere, not a blank page. Have a real USAJOBS announcement open while you listen so each point lands against something specific.

entries.org: USO × ACP — MilSpouse Connections That Open Doors
entries.what: A free one-hour webinar run by the USO with American Corporate Partners (ACP) on mentorship — how to find a mentor, build professional connections and turn them into work. The webinar is the doorway to ACP's own mentoring programme, which is the thing worth the hour.
facts: Wednesday 4 November 2026 · 11:00 AM Eastern · 10:00 Central · 9:00 Mountain · 8:00 Pacific

Published audience is military spouses, active duty, National Guard and Reservists. I could not open the registration form to confirm whether veterans and retirees appear as affiliation options, so check the form before assuming either way.

A free mentoring programme that pairs you one-to-one with a professional from a major company for twelve months. Not a webinar series and not a portal — a named person in your field, for a year, at no cost.

ACP does not take every military spouse. Their own criteria cover four situations: spouses of active duty service members; spouses of veterans who left active duty within the past 12 months; surviving spouses of post-9/11 veterans; and spouses of severely wounded post-9/11 veterans who are the household's primary financial provider, or returning to work in that role.
Open to currently serving and recently separated veterans, including Reserve and National Guard, who have 180 days or more on active duty orders since 9/11.
Daylight saving ended 1 November, so 11 AM Eastern that week is EST, not EDT. Your Zoom confirmation shows the start in your own time zone — trust that over any graphic.
The value of mentorship, how to find the right mentor for your goals, building meaningful professional connections, standing out as a candidate, and how mentorship bridges into employment.

entries.what: Two halves. An in-person Retiree Summit, Career Fair and MWR Expo at JEB Little Creek on Friday 30 October, and a Virtual Retiree Summit of daily webinars from Monday 2 to Friday 6 November. Run by Fleet & Family Support and MWR. Free.
facts: Friday 30 October 2026 · 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM Eastern · JEB Little Creek, Rockwell Hall Gym, Virginia Beach. Over 30 employers on site, plus veteran resources, a health fair with free flu shots, and the MWR expo.
Military retirees, transitioning military, family members and surviving spouses.

Little Creek is a working installation. If you hold a DoD ID you can drive on. If you do not, you need a visitor pass and it is not a same-day walk-up: visitors 17 and over complete SECNAV Form 5512/1, submit it by encrypted email to JEBLCFS_BASE_ACCESS@US.NAVY.MIL or drop it at the Gate 3 Visitor Control Center, and allow time for security screening. Approved guests show a state-issued ID or passport at the gate. Call the base before making the drive.
Monday 2 to Friday 6 November 2026. A webinar a day, online, no base access needed. This is the half anyone can attend.

Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) · Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) · Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) · TRICARE for Retirees · Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP) · Department of Veterans Affairs · Social Security Administration · Navy Household Goods · Employment Opportunities.
Webinars need sign-up through the summit page — pick the sessions you want before Monday rather than on the morning. The in-person event is listed as open attendance.
SBP and DFAS are the two sessions that cost families real money when they are misunderstood. If you only sit in on one, make it one of those.

entries.org: ACT Now Education × SANS — Veterans Day BootUp CTF
entries.what: A free 72-hour Capture the Flag cybersecurity competition over Veterans Day, run by the SANS Institute and sponsored by ACT Now Education. Built for beginner and intermediate players — no prior cyber experience needed. Top three win a SANS Skills Quest subscription.
facts: CTF registration closes Monday 9 November 2026 at 12:00 PM Eastern. No late sign-ups.
The deadline falls BEFORE the orientation webinar on Tuesday 10 November. The obvious plan — attend the webinar, then sign up — does not work. Register first, learn second.

Registering for the webinar does not enter you in the CTF. Register for the webinar first, then open your SANS account dashboard and follow the prompt to register separately for the CTF on Ranges.io. Do only the first and you will have nothing to log into on Wednesday.
Wednesday 11 November 2026 at 9:00 AM Eastern to Saturday 14 November 2026 at 9:00 AM Eastern. 72 hours, played at your own pace.

Ranked by hit rate — the fewest total attempts across the challenges you complete. Not the most flags, not the fastest finish. Speed only breaks a tie. Every wrong submission counts against you, so read the challenge and submit once rather than brute-forcing it. This is the single thing a first-timer is most likely to get wrong.
Service members, veterans, military spouses, dependents, and anyone curious about cybersecurity. Free. Virtual.
Top three by hit rate each receive a SANS Skills Quest subscription. Previous SANS BootUp CTF winners may compete but are not eligible to win a prize.

An older SANS landing page still shows a 3 November deadline and a 60-hour window ending 13 November. That page is stale. The dates here come from the SANS webcast page and the SANS press announcement, which agree with each other.

entries.what: Free monthly peer support groups for military and veteran caregivers — the person doing the caring, not the person being cared for. One hour on Zoom, facilitated by the Foundation's Mental Wellness Specialist. Three groups run, each on its own Tuesday of the month.
facts: Any military or veteran caregiver aged 18 or over whose situation matches the group topic. If you manage someone's VA appointments, track their medication, work around their bad days or hold the household together while they cannot — that is caregiving, whether or not you have ever used the word. A lot of people who qualify do not think the label applies to them.

Caring for someone with post-traumatic stress — first Tuesday of the month, 5:00 PM Eastern. Caring for someone sixty and under — second Tuesday. Caring for someone over sixty — third Tuesday. In November 2026 those fall on the 3rd, 10th and 17th.
One hour on Zoom. Free. Facilitated by Rebecca Mullaney, the Foundation's Mental Wellness Specialist. No commitment to attend every month — come when you can.

Care Groups are not mental health counselling and not therapy, and the Foundation states that on its own page rather than letting people find out in the session. Peer support sits alongside clinical care; it does not replace it.

The Foundation publishes the downsides too, which is unusual: reflecting on your own caregiving, or hearing others describe theirs, can surface difficult memories and emotions; and confidentiality is expected of everyone in the group but cannot be guaranteed. Worth knowing before you join rather than after.
Daylight saving ended 1 November 2026, so 5:00 PM Eastern that week is EST, not EDT. Your confirmation shows the start in your own time zone.
If it is heavier than that
A peer group is not crisis support. The Veterans Crisis Line is available to caregivers and family members as well as veterans: dial 988 then press 1, or text 838255.

entries.what: A free in-person resource fair run by the Disabled Veterans National Foundation, bringing together employment, housing, financial, benefits and health organisations — plus free services you can walk out with the same day. DMV area only.
facts: Monday 9 November 2026 · 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM · College Park Marriott Hotel & Conference Center, 3501 University Blvd E, Hyattsville, MD 20783. Free entry, free parking.
Two start times are published for this one: the registration page says 9:00 AM and the event graphic says 9:30 AM. Plan for 9:00 and you cannot be caught out.
A DD214 or a VA card is required. Not a description of your service — a document. Pre-registration is encouraged through the ticket page.

milConnect is the quick route but it needs a premium DS Logon; an ID.me or My HealtheVet login will not open your records there, which catches people out. A National Archives request runs one to three weeks. If you hold a VA card but not the DD214, call DVNF on 202-737-0522 before making the trip rather than finding out at the door.
Employment opportunities, housing assistance, financial assistance, veteran benefits, and physical and mental health support.

Work attire, haircuts, basic manicure, medical, dental, comfort kits, food, refreshments, gift cards and a raffle. The work attire and the haircut together amount to an interview you can actually turn up to.
Sold out. Attendee registration is still open, but an organisation hoping to exhibit has missed the window.

entries.what: A free 20-week Microsoft training programme for military spouses, toward a systems administrator role. Live and virtual. Microsoft ran a program brief on 2 November 2026 and the recording stays available, so the information is not time-locked — but the application windows are.
facts: MSSA–Military Spouse is a 20-week programme on one track: server and cloud administration, toward a systems administrator role. It covers scripting and automation, networking, identity and access management, cloud administration, and Azure and AI fundamentals.

Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM Pacific, live and virtual, with optional office hours either side. Around fifteen people to a class. This is a full-time commitment for five months, not an evening course. Anyone who works, cares for someone, or expects to move house mid-programme should work out whether those hours are possible before applying.

A LinkedIn Learning path — Networking and Administration Fundamentals, about 20 hours — is required, and it needs LinkedIn Premium. Eligible members of the military community get LinkedIn Premium free for a year, so claim that rather than paying for it. See the LinkedIn Premium entry on this list.

The programme offers role-search support and networking with corporate partners. It does not guarantee an interview with Microsoft or with a hiring partner. Worth asking what the actual placement rate is.

Microsoft's own pages disagree with each other on the application window: one place shows September 20–27 2027 for a February 2028 cohort, another shows September 20–27 2026 for the same programme. Do not plan around either. Ask Microsoft directly when the next window opens and closes.

Monday 2 November 2026, two sessions on Microsoft Teams — 12:00 PM Eastern and 4:00 PM Eastern. Session 1: aka.ms/MilSpouseSession1. Session 2: aka.ms/MilSpouseSession2. A recording is available on demand at lnkd.in/gWvVKc3d, so the brief itself is not a deadline.

The separate MSSA programme for transitioning service members, veterans and retirees is open to all US and UK MoD branches. Active duty applicants need a separation date within 180 days of the programme start and must speak to their local SkillBridge manager first.

entries.what: Ten paid subscriptions the military community can use at no cost through the Morale, Welfare and Recreation digital library — O'Reilly Learning, EBSCO LearningExpress, Tutor.com, Universal Class, Mango Languages, Libby/OverDrive, The Wall Street Journal, Consumer Reports, Ancestry Library Edition and Gale OneFile: Vocations and Careers. One login covers all of them.
facts: Under DoD Instruction 1015.10: active duty; Reserve and National Guard; retirees; Medal of Honor recipients; veterans with a 100% service-connected disability; and eligible dependents with an ID card.

A veteran rated below 100% service-connected does not get access on veteran status by itself. This is the same rule that governs on-base MWR privileges, not a decision the library makes. Worth knowing before you create an account.

DoD and Coast Guard civilians, both appropriated and non-appropriated fund, qualify while stationed outside the United States. Stateside, access depends on the individual resource. Local nationals sign in with a library card number; contractors have to go through the Contact Us link.

Go to dodmwrlibraries.org and pick your service's portal, then sign in with your DoD ID number and date of birth. Not a CAC and not a DS Logon — the portal checks you against DEERS. Then open Digital Collections, A to Z.

If your ID card shows an SSN instead of a DoD ID number, enter 0000000000 in the DoD ID field and then the last four digits of your SSN on the next page. This is published on their own FAQ and almost nobody repeats it. It is the step that stops older retirees getting in.

O'Reilly Learning carries technology, AI, cybersecurity and certification prep — the full library, not a sampler. If you are studying Security+, AWS or Azure, look there before buying a course. EBSCO LearningExpress carries the practice tests people usually pay for separately.

Consumer Reports is blocked by some military network filters, and single sign-on resources can fail on military or high-security networks. Try from a personal connection before concluding you do not have access. Offline reading works for most but not all magazines, e-books and audiobooks.

Tutor.com appears in this collection but carries its own eligibility rules on top of the library's. There is also a separate, directly funded route at military.tutor.com — see the Tutor.com entry on this list, which has different rules again.

Which resources appear differs by service portal and changes over time. If something listed here is missing from your A to Z, check another service portal or ask your MWR library before assuming it has gone.

entries.what: Heroes Sail Free — $0 base cruise fare for the first two guests in an interior stateroom on Margaritaville at Sea Islander or Paradise, for verified GOVX members. A separate offer takes 20% off retail for guests one through four.
facts: Active and former U.S. military, plus first responders, educators, medical personnel and government employees. You must be a verified GOVX member at the time of booking.
$0 cruise fare for the first and second guests only, in an interior stateroom on Islander or Paradise. Third and fourth guests pay prevailing retail rates. There is no single-traveller offer.
Auto-assigned “We Pick” staterooms only — you do not choose the room. Capacity-controlled, select sail dates, first come first served.
Taxes, fees and port expenses are assessed per guest and are due at booking, plus gratuities and onboard charges. A free fare is not a free invoice.
Distinct from the free cabin: 20% off the retail fare for guests one through four. Does not apply to single travellers, and blackout dates may apply based on stateroom availability.

entries.what: All-expenses-paid vacations for severely combat-wounded service members — medically retired, former or active — and their immediate family. Nominations are accepted year-round and reviewed quarterly.
facts: Generally a combined disability rating of 80–100% or greater, with a single physical disability rating of 30% or more, for injuries or wounds sustained during combat.

Blindness or loss of vision; severe burns; spinal cord injury or paralysis; traumatic brain injury; or loss of one limb, arm or leg, or more. This list is the real gate — the rating alone does not decide it.
The organization describes the trips as all-expenses-paid but does not itemise what that includes anywhere on its site. Ask for the list in writing before you plan a week around it.

Anyone may nominate. Referrals come from past recipients, VA personnel and active-duty personnel, as well as direct contact. The nominee completes the V4W application. New vacations are considered quarterly.
The organization states plainly that there are far more candidates than available vacations, and that no application is guaranteed a trip.

entries.what: Sponsored restorative getaways for military members, veterans, first responders and Gold Star families. Applications are open year-round and the board of directors makes the final selection.
facts: Four eligibility categories on the application: Military, Veteran, First Responder, and Gold Star Family. Verification may require service records, a veteran ID, first responder credentials or Gold Star documentation.

Individual review, then verification of service and eligibility, then a recommendation from an Application Review Committee, then a final decision by the board of directors weighed on mission, funding, capacity and expected restorative impact.
The organization states its getaways are intended to complement, not replace, professional medical or mental health treatment. Worth knowing before you apply on someone else's behalf.
Trip format, how many family members are included, and whether transportation is covered are not stated on the application page. Ask before making any plans.

entries.what: Seven donated nights in a condominium, typically Orange Beach or Gulf Shores, Alabama, or northwest Florida, for veterans who deployed to a combat zone after 9/11 and their families. Trips run in spring and fall.
facts: Served in the United States military, any branch and any rank, and deployed to a combat zone on or after 11 September 2001.
Seven nights in a property donated by owners and rental management companies, typically coastal Alabama — Orange Beach or Gulf Shores — or northwest Florida, in spring or fall.
The most recent returning deployers, within 12 months, always have priority. Registering first does not guarantee selection.
The organization may offer gas cards, gift certificates for necessities or meals so that money does not stop a family coming. It is not advertised — ask when you register.
The live registration form is still labelled 2025 and the page states no open or close date. Confirm the current intake with the organization before counting on a trip.

entries.what: A two-night family condominium weekend at St. James, North Carolina, with meals, gas money and a family photo session, for active-duty families. The 2027 application window opens 1 December 2026.
facts: Active-duty service members and their families, any branch and any location. Veterans are not listed. The weekend is for military members, spouses and their children — other relatives and friends are not covered.

Two nights in a two- or three-bedroom condominium at St. James, near Southport and Oak Island. Friday dinner and both breakfasts prepared and in the condo on arrival, restaurant coupons for two lunches and Saturday dinner, money for gas to drive there, a family photo session, gifts and one Saturday activity.
Applications for 2027 begin 1 December 2026. The organization contacts applicant families from 1 January 2027 to schedule. No closing date is published.

Not first come first served. First priority goes to personnel separated from their families and recently deployed to a combat zone or similar area; selections are then based on rank and deployment length.
The rental condominiums cannot accommodate pets, and weekend parking or storage for boats and trailers is not available.

entries.what: Six-day therapeutic retreats, Friday to Wednesday, for military and veteran families and couples — all branches including Coast Guard, all eras, Guard and Reserve and first responders included. Lodging, meals and activities are covered; travel is not.
facts: Active duty, retirees, veterans, Reserve and Guard, and first responders; all branches including Coast Guard, all eras. For families and couples — space is limited to immediate family or the one person who supports you. Solo attendees are referred to partner organizations.
Six days, Friday to Wednesday. Your own cabin, lodge room or duplex with linens and towels, all meals, activities and equipment such as helmets, and professional family portraits.

A $100 commitment fee by PayPal secures your retreat date. It is refunded on successful completion of the entire six-day retreat, and the wrap-up survey must be submitted before you leave the retreat centre on the last day.

Cancel less than one month before your retreat date and the $100 is forfeited, you must wait two years before reapplying, and a $200 commitment fee is then required. This is published and almost nobody repeats it.

Transportation to and from the retreat, souvenirs and personal items. Locations are remote and rideshare is not recommended. Families with financial need can work with the intake coordinator on getting there.
All classes and workshops are mandatory. Recreation activities are optional.

entries.org: Red, White & Blue Summit — Hampton Roads, Fall 2026
entries.what: Three free in-person events in Norfolk on 18 and 19 November for service members, veterans, military spouses and families, run by the Center for Military and Family Advancement, part of the Hampton Roads Workforce Council. Thursday is the hiring day — meet employers in the morning, fifteen-minute interviews the same afternoon.
facts: 9:30 AM to 1:30 PM EST at Vista Point Conference Center, 1754 Massey Hughes Drive, Norfolk. Schools, childcare, housing, benefits, SkillBridge, apprenticeship pathways, training and certifications.

5:30 to 8:00 PM EST at Waters Edge Winery, 6464 Hampton Blvd, Norfolk. Off base, so no gate to clear. No childcare provided. Eventbrite lists it as “Red, White & Brew (Fall Edition) Southside” — search that exact name or the ticket will not come up.

9:00 AM to 3:00 PM EST at Vista Point. Employers on the floor 9 to 12, fifteen-minute interviews 1 to 3. Free professional headshots, résumé and profile help, and SKYBOX one-to-one mentoring for E-7 to O-6 and experienced military spouses. Children welcome.

Vista Point sits inside Naval Station Norfolk, so both daytime events are on base. Without a DoD ID, Navy Region Mid-Atlantic requires a REAL ID-compliant driver's licence, state ID card or US passport, plus the SECNAV 5512/1 base access registration form, plus a pass from the Pass & ID office.

Naval Station Norfolk suspended its Trusted Traveler Program in March 2026, so someone holding a CAC can no longer vouch for passengers in their vehicle. Visitors need a sponsor and a valid visitor pass. That is the most recent published policy as of this check.

The organizer has not published a gate-access process for this event, and they may well have one arranged. Call the Center for Military and Family Advancement on 757-807-0423 and ask, days ahead — not on the morning of the 19th.

45+ organizations scheduled for the 19th. Named so far: General Dynamics Mission Systems, HII Mission Technologies, Newport News Shipbuilding, Norfolk Naval Shipyard, Dominion Energy, USAA, Fiserv, Epsilon Systems Solutions, Wawa, City of Norfolk, City of Virginia Beach, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
Each event has its own Eventbrite ticket — register for every one you plan to attend. All three are free. This is the fall edition of a quarterly series that ran previously as the 757 Career Summit.

entries.org: Google Launchpad for Veterans — Gen AI Leader 2026
entries.what: A free two-day virtual Google Cloud Gen AI Leader training on 12 and 13 November 2026, hosted by ROI Training, ending in a complimentary certification exam voucher. Open to U.S. and Canada military veterans and service members. Registration needs the access code ACTNowEducation.
facts: U.S. and Canada military veterans and service members. No prior technical experience is required — Gen AI Leader is the non-technical track.

12 and 13 November 2026, virtual, hosted by ROI Training. Interactive training sessions plus a panel discussion with veterans from Google. Start times and the time zone are not stated on the published material.
Two days of training, a complimentary Gen AI Leader exam voucher, two follow-on exam prep sessions, and a chance at a pair of Google socks — in 2025 the socks went to the first 500 people who passed.

Register with ACTNowEducation. The published steps are: click Sign Me Up, select “Continue without email”, enter your email address, enter the access code, then finish the remaining prompts. Steps two and three look contradictory and are meant to be followed in that order.

Attending earns a voucher, not a certification. The Gen AI Leader exam is booked and sat separately, and passing it is what earns the credential. A voucher left unredeemed is the most common way this ends in nothing.

The exam prep session dates and the voucher expiry date are not on the flyer or on anything Google has published for the 2026 cohort. Ask for both at registration and diary the expiry the day the voucher lands.

2024 ran as Cloud Digital Leader. In 2025 the event was 13–14 November, prep sessions were 17 and 21 November, and Google encouraged taking the exam between 21 November and 19 December without publishing a voucher expiry. Useful as a shape for what to expect, not as 2026 dates.

entries.what: 82 restaurants appear on the Veterans Day lists circulating this year. 28 were confirmed when ACT Now Education compiled its guide on 29 October; 15 more were reported by deal trackers without chain confirmation, and 39 gave free food in 2025 with no 2026 terms announced. Re-checked against VA News and Military.com on 8 November.
facts: 28 chains as of the guide's compilation date: Applebee's, Bob Evans, Chili's, Cotton Patch Cafe, Denny's, Golden Corral, Hoss's, In-N-Out, Lazy Dog, Mission BBQ, Olive Garden, Pilot/Flying J, Red Robin, Sheetz, Sizzler, Texas Roadhouse, White Castle, IHOP, Cracker Barrel, Bonefish Grill, Outback, Starbucks, Krispy Kreme, Dunkin', 151 Coffee, Marzoni's, Chipotle and Rubio's.
VA News has since confirmed eight more: Red Lobster, Shake Shack, Yard House, Smashburger, Freddy's, Bar Louie, Biscuit Belly and World of Beer. Any list dated late October is already behind.
Veterans Canteen Service at VA medical centers runs on the 10th, a day before Veterans Day. Worth knowing if you have an appointment that Tuesday.
A voucher, not a meal on the day. Collected between 11 AM and 2 PM on the 11th and redeemed on a later visit, good through 31 May 2027. Confirmed on Military.com.
Denny's runs 5 AM to noon. Sizzler until 4 PM. Golden Corral does not start until 4 PM. Outback covers both the 10th and the 11th. Hoss's $10-off-$40 voucher is good to 25 November.
Not all of it is free
Chipotle needs a $5 purchase. Rubio's is buy-one-get-one with code VETS26. Drinks, tax and tip are usually not included anywhere, and franchises can opt out of the whole thing.
Military ID, VA card, DD-214, or the veteran designation on a driver's licence. Most offers are dine-in at participating locations. Starbucks includes spouses; most do not.
The guide states the free meal is for the service member and that family pays. Neither VA News nor Military.com says that. Ask when you call rather than assuming either way.
A chain confirming nationally does not bind the branch near you. One phone call beats a wasted drive, and it is the only step that makes any of this reliable.

entries.org: Service to Success — Virtual Military & Federal Hiring Fair
entries.what: A free three-hour virtual hiring fair on Friday 13 November 2026, 3:00 to 6:00 PM EST, run by Service to Success with ACT Now Education and hosted on Zoom Events. For veterans, transitioning service members, military spouses, SkillBridge candidates and the federal community.
facts: 3:00 to 6:00 PM EST — 2 PM CT, 1 PM MT, noon PT. Three hours, not a drop-in. The intro keynote runs 3 to 4 PM and the registration page says to join there first; a help chat runs 4 to 6 PM alongside the fair.

The full event name is the Virtual Military AND Federal Hiring Fair. Most graphics drop the federal half. Open to veterans, transitioning service members, military spouses, SkillBridge candidates and the federal community.

Amazon, Navy Federal Credit Union, ManTech, V2X, T-Mobile, TEKsystems, CHRISTUS Health, Leaf Home, ARA, FDM Group, and GuidePoint Security — the last of which is named on the registration page and on none of the circulating graphics.

The organiser states companies are still signing up and that the final list of registered employers is emailed to attendees before the day. Do not skip the event because your industry is missing from a flyer.
IT and cybersecurity; engineering and defense; healthcare; operations, finance and sales.

The servicetosuccess.com/HiringFair link redirects to Zoom Events, not to their own site. Register with a Zoom account or with an email address. Free. Zoom restricts registration to a listed set of countries, which may matter if you are OCONUS.
The confirmation email arrives immediately after registering and is the one that carries the final employer list. The organiser flags that it often lands in spam.
What to ask on the day
Which of your roles fit what I have done; what am I missing to qualify; what should I do next to apply. A conversation gives you the gap analysis an application never will.

entries.org: ACT Now Education — SkillBridge: three tech roles
entries.what: Three open DoD SkillBridge placements sourced by ACT Now Education, for transitioning service members in their final 180 days of service: Site IT Support Technician (Flowery Branch, GA), Network Test Lab Engineer (Roseville, CA hybrid or Andover, MA), and Junior Data Engineer (Cincinnati, OH). Applications are by email, rolling, with no posted closing date.
facts: Site IT Support Technician — Flowery Branch, GA. Network Test Lab Engineer — Roseville, CA (hybrid) or Andover, MA. Junior Data Engineer — Cincinnati, OH.

The Department of Defense remains responsible for all pay and benefits for the duration of the placement, and the industry partner receives the participant at no cost. Any hourly or annual figure attached to one of these roles is the job's own rate, applicable if and when the placement converts to employment — not compensation during the 180 days. Only the Junior Data Engineer listing labels its figure correctly, as "after SkillBridge." Ask when the listed rate starts before accepting.

SkillBridge sits inside the final 180 days of service. It is not open to someone 6 to 12 months out, who can plan and apply but cannot yet participate. Participation must also occur within 180 days of discharge.

180 continuous days of active duty already served. Approval from the first field grade commander with Article 15 authority. Open to all four branches plus the Guard and Reserve on qualifying active-duty orders.
A placement more than 50 miles from the service member's duty station requires specific commander authorisation. All three of these roles are tied to a named city, so this applies to most applicants.
Industry partners generally cannot provide gifts or compensation, but may offer subsistence, lodging or travel subsidies where these are offered to all similar trainees.
Email nicole.dhanraj@actnoweducation.org with the job title and your location preference. Rolling, no posted deadline.

When does the listed rate start — during the placement or only on conversion? Is there a conversion offer at the end, and what has the conversion rate been? Will the host support a placement more than 50 miles from the duty station?

entries.org: Wounded Warrior Project × USAA — Warrior Secure Start
entries.what: A $1,000 financial empowerment grant for veterans in their first 24 months after military service, run by Wounded Warrior Project with USAA funding. Complete a financial education course with a WWP Financial Readiness specialist, submit the certificate, and the grant is paid into your bank account. Nothing to repay. Registration with WWP is free and is the prerequisite.
facts: The common assumption that WWP is only for the visibly wounded is the main barrier to this grant. WWP's registration page states that a visible injury or combat-related injury is not required, and sets eligibility at having served on or after 11 September 2001.

Veterans who served on or after 11 September 2001; active-duty service members; service members preparing to transition; eligible National Guard and Reserve members; and family members, caregivers and others in a warrior's support system. Registration is free.

You can join WWP while still serving or while preparing to transition. Because the grant window is the first 24 months after service, registering early means the window is spent using the program rather than joining it.

$1,000, one time, described by USAA as purpose-built for veterans during the first 24 months after military service. Announced 9 July 2026 as part of a $5M, five-year USAA commitment expected to support more than 4,000 veterans.

Paid directly into the veteran's bank account after the financial education course is completed and the certificate is submitted. Usable for emergency savings, paying down debt, or another financial goal. No repayment.

Not a self-serve form. The veteran meets a WWP Financial Readiness specialist who reviews their situation before directing them to the course modules. The program is aimed at veterans experiencing financial strain, and grants run in the hundreds per year rather than unlimited.

An 80% quiz pass mark, two coaching sessions and a 60-day completion window circulate with this program but appear on neither USAA's announcement nor WWP's Financial Readiness page, which does not name Warrior Secure Start at all. One published account describes course modules with three classes. Confirm actual requirements with the specialist at enrollment.
Register at woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/wwp-registration, or call 888.WWP.ALUM (888.997.2586). The WWP Resource Center can confirm which documents are needed and answer eligibility questions.
